4. FETAL MONITORING DURING LABOUR

FHR monitoring is a guidance tool on fetal condition and not a diagnostic test.

Findings of FHR monitoring should be assessed along with clinical picture

Decisions are based on clinical picture along with FHR monitoring but never alone on FHR findings.

Women’s decision should be respected

Maintain one to one support

Increased intervention with continuous CTG as compared to intermittent auscultation.

Initial assessment during labour:

Assessment of risks

Review ANC record

Women’s preferences and method of fetal assessment discussed with her during antenatal period.

Discuss with women that risk assessment is a continuous process so, FHR monitoring tool may change during the course of labour.

Intermittent Auscultation – IA:

Offer to low risk women

Use either pinard stethoscope or Doppler USG

Carry out Intermittent Auscultation after a palpated contraction

For 1 min

Every 15 min in 1st stage and every 5 min in 2nd stage

Record o Partogram as single rate

Record accelerations and decelerations if heard.

Palpate maternal pulse and record 1 hourly and more oftenly if there are any concerns.

Ensure differentiation between the maternal and fetal heartbeat.

No fetal heart beat => urgent real time USG assessment.

Concerns about differentiating between fetal and maternal heart rates => seek help and consider changing the method of FHR monitoring.

In 2nd stage it is easier to mistakenly auscultate maternal rather than FHR

Important Consideration while Reviewing CTG:

Evaluate changes on trace over time

Document any change from previous review

Review changes alongside existing or new intrapartum risk factors

Think about possible reason for any change and take into account whole clinical picture in formulating ongoing care.

Normal CTG trace indicate that baby is coping well with labour

Changes to FHR during labour are common and don’t necessarily cause concern, however they may represent fetal compromise.

If CTG trace changes or is not normal there will be less certainly about the condition of the baby

Accelerations:

Transient in FHR of 15bpm or more lasting 15 sec or more

Presence of accelerations even with reduced variability is reassuring.

Absence of accelerations on an otherwise normal CTG trace does not indicate fetal acidosis.

Categorization of CTG traces:

Normal

No amber or no red feature

All 4 features are white.

Suspicious:

Any 1 feature amber

Pathological

Any feature red or

2 or more features are amber.

Special consideration for CTG traces in 2nd stage of labour:

Interpretation more challenging in 2nd stage

Keep low threshold for seeking 2nd opinion

Differentiate FHR from MHR every 5 min

Consider scalp electrode if there is concern

about confusing FHR and MHR.

Accelerations are most likely to be maternal pulse

If there are deceleration, look for other signs of hypoxia like in baseline FHR or reduction in variability.

Hypoxia is more common and more rapid in active 2nd stage

FHR > 20bPm from baseline or more from start of labour is labelled as red feature in active.

CTG concern in 2nd stage.

 

 

Obtain obstetric review

Discourage Pushing

Discontinue oxytocin infusion unless birth is imminent

Agree and document CTG trace.

Record keeping for CTG:

Set date and time clock correctly on machine

Set paper speed at 1cm/ min

Correct labelling with women’s name, DOB, NHS Number, Pulse rate @ start of monitoring and date of CTG
